title: Vishal:
headline: A Syrian tailor thought he'd be home in a few days. Nine years later, one loan put him back in business.
story: Vishal tells the story of a refugee he met in Amman, Jordan. He had a successful tailoring business in Syria. When the war came he left, thinking he'd be back home in a few days. Eight or nine years later he was still in Amman, with nothing, and could do nothing.
Through one of the very few Kiva partners that lend to refugees, he got a loan. The video lands on the pride on his face: he was back doing what he did best. Hopeful, never political.
do: Open cold on “he thought he'd be back home in a few days”, with <q>Home in a few days</q> on screen.
Trim his hesitations tightly. Cover every trim with the bridge B-roll.
Name super after the hook: “Vishal Ghotge” / “CEO of Kiva”.
Land on the pride line and end there.
Match the colour of the last lines: he walks into shade at the end of the take.
dont: Do not put the borrower's name on screen until Brit confirms the spelling.
No war images, maps or politics.
No name plate, logo or fade at 0:00.
No crew talk at the end (“How did it look?”, the shade discussion).
No big lime captions. Brit's caption spec only.
